title: Only parity is rebuilt by native gadgets of its own copies (three places)
claim: Knots on three bits are the 34 relations in which every two coordinates are unconstrained, other than the full cube. A native gadget is a connected loopless network of m >= 2 copies of one knot, each placed in any coordinate order, with variables identified in pairs between distinct copies and three legs; its relation is the projection onto the legs. Theorem 1: for the two parity knots every native gadget gives back the knot. Theorem 3: for every other knot K every native gadget excludes strictly fewer leg tuples than K: none if K has no wire face (the 8 atoms and the 4 knots of not-all-equal type), at most one if K excludes two tuples, at most two if it excludes three, and at most one unless a copy carries two legs. Corollary 4: no non-parity knot is rebuilt, and repeated substitution of a knot by a native gadget of its copies reaches the full relation within three levels. Proposition 5: no three-bit knot has its coordinate symmetry group inside the rotations of a cyclic order, so placements never orient a vertex; among four-bit knots some do.
failure_conditions: A connected loopless native gadget of copies of a non-parity three-bit knot whose leg relation excludes at least as many tuples as the knot, or more than the stated bound for its type.
A native gadget of a parity knot whose leg relation is not that parity knot.
A three-bit knot whose coordinate symmetry group lies inside the rotations of a cyclic order.
An excluded leg tuple whose pinned network is not a cactus of odd wire cycles with a leg beyond every bridge.
foundation_claim_scope: Set-level relations (allowed tuples, not counts) on three bits that pass K1-K3 (the 34 knots); native gadgets are connected, loopless, with every internal variable in exactly two copies of one knot; the orientation statement compares coordinate symmetry groups with rotation groups of cyclic orders. Exhaustive checks cover gadgets of three and five copies; the theorems are proved for every size.

validation.status: checked: 34 knots and their types; three-bit symmetry groups all contain a transposition (none orients a vertex), 96 of 742 four-bit knots orient one; exhaustive census of native gadgets with 3 and 5 copies (11 shapes, every placement): parity rebuilt by every gadget, no other knot rebuilt, bounds 0/1/2 hold and are attained, flow strictly decreasing with longest chain 3; the cactus and odd-wire-cycle structure verified for all 798 excluded leg tuples; 6120 random evaluations with 7, 9 and 11 copies; controls fire (self-gluing rebuilds non-parity knots, all-equal is rebuilt, a mutated bound fails). The theorems are proved in prose for every gadget size from NATIVE-HARDNESS-20261024-001B Lemma 1 and Corollary 3; no human or external review
